title: Layer edit lock timeout may drop position updates
description:
## Summary

If two refresh cycles complete within the 10-second lock timeout, one update will fail with `LayerLockError`. This could cause dropped position updates during high-activity periods with many devices.

## Location

`controllers/layer_managers/tracking_manager.py` lines 573-652

## Technical Details

```python
if not self.acquire_layer_edit_lock(timeout=10.0):
    raise LayerLockError(
        f"{self.CURRENT_LAYER_NAME} - concurrent update in progress. "
        "Please wait for the current operation to complete."
    )
```

With 30+ devices generating large datasets, layer transactions may take longer than expected. If refresh interval is shorter than transaction time, updates will be dropped.

## Impact

- **Severity**: HIGH
- Position updates dropped during high-activity periods
- User notification shown but positions remain stale
- More likely with 20+ devices and slow I/O

## Acceptance Criteria

- Lock acquisition logged with timestamp for debugging
- Consider extending timeout for known large-dataset scenarios
- Implement retry mechanism with backoff
close_reason: Added retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts, 5s base timeout). Timeout scales with position count (+1s per 50 positions, capped at 30s). Detailed logging on retry attempts and when lock takes >1s.

title: Phase 4: Replay Data Semantics (Current Positions from Breadcrumbs)
description:
# Phase 4: Replay Data Semantics (Current + Breadcrumbs Alignment)

## Goal
Make replay consistent by deriving "current" positions from breadcrumbs.

## Problem
Currently:
- Breadcrumbs: Historical (uses replay window)
- Current positions: Live (ignores replay window)

This creates a dangerous mismatch: historical trails with live markers.

## Design Decision (from Phase 0)
Option A: Derive Current from Breadcrumbs (Client-Side)

## Implementation Plan

### A. Provider Helper Method (providers/traccar_http.py)
Add utility to derive current from breadcrumbs:

- Use parse_iso to compare timestamps safely (timezone/microseconds)
- Skip entries without device_id or ts

### B. Task Modification (providers/tasks.py)
Modify TraccarRefreshTask.run() to handle replay mode:

- Use an explicit replay_enabled flag (do not infer from until_iso alone)
- In replay mode:
  - Do NOT call get_current()
  - Fetch breadcrumbs for the window
  - Derive current from breadcrumbs
  - Consider disabling last-good cache fallback for replay (avoid mixing live cache)

### C. Edge Cases
- Device with no positions in window: no current marker
- Empty breadcrumbs: current empty
- Multiple devices: latest per device

### D. Logging
- Log replay window and mode explicitly

## TDD Test Cases

Unit tests:
- derive_current_from_breadcrumbs handles empty input
- single device latest selected
- multiple devices latest selected
- missing device_id skipped

Integration tests (QGIS):
- replay mode uses derived current (get_current not used or result overridden)
- normal mode still uses live current
- replay mode does not fall back to live last-good cache

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replay mode: current positions derived from breadcrumbs
- Normal mode: unchanged behavior
- parse_iso used for timestamp comparisons
- Explicit replay flag used in task
- Tests cover derivation and task behavior

## Files Changed
- providers/traccar_http.py - add derive_current_from_breadcrumbs
- providers/tasks.py - replay semantics and flag
- tests/test_traccar_provider.py - unit tests
- tests/test_traccar_task_replay.py - integration tests

## Risk Assessment
MEDIUM - changes refresh task behavior
SAFETY - removes live/historical mismatch

DEPENDS ON

  -> SAR-d39o: Phase 2: Replay Validation Hardening
  -> SAR-qt3y: Phase 0: Design Decision

  <- SAR-z24h: Phase 7: Test Coverage

title: Review global vendor injection impact on other plugins
description:
**LOW PRIORITY STABILITY RISK**: sartracker.py forcefully rewrites `sys.path` (line 36) and purges `requests/urllib3/...` from `sys.modules` (line 128) at import time.

This can break other QGIS plugins that already imported `requests` or rely on different versions. During active rescue operations, other plugins might be in use (basemap, geocoding, device integrations).

Current approach attempts to ensure bundled vendor stack is used, but affects global interpreter.

Suggested mitigations:
- Only adjust sys.path locally around import calls
- Avoid global sys.modules purge
- Add guard to only adjust when requests not yet imported
- Document compatibility behavior in diagnostics panel

Reference: `FINDINGS/findings.md` Finding #1 for details.
acceptance_criteria:
- Impact assessment documented
- Decision on mitigation approach
- If changed: no regression in vendor imports
- If not changed: risk documented in diagnostics
close_reason: Impact assessment complete. Decision: Keep current vendor injection approach because (1) it ensures reliable network requests for life-safety operations, (2) fallback mechanism mitigates hard failures, (3) changing it risks regressions. Risk documented in diagnostics panel tooltip explaining potential impact on other plugins and workaround (load other plugins first).
